blocks.title: Front matter
blocks.content:
MINISTRY OF HEALTH
National Expanded Programme 
on Immunization
GOVERNMENT OF UGANDA
Vision
 
To ensure that the 
Ugandan population is free 
of vaccine-preventable 
diseases
Mission
Goal
To contribute to the 
overall objective of the 
HSDP in reducing 
morbidity, mortality and 
disability due to vaccine 
preventable diseases, so 
that they are no longer of 
public health importance
To ensure that every 
child and high-risk group 
is fully vaccinated with 
high quality and effective 
vaccines against the 
target diseases 
according to 
recommended strategies

UNEPI objectives, numbered: 01 Increase access and demand for immunization services; 02 Ensure availability of potent and effective vaccines; 03 Build EPI management capacity at all levels; 04 Monitor disease trends and programme performance; 05 Formulate policy, standards and guidelines.

'EPI Target Diseases (14 VPDs)': a syringe illustration with callouts naming Rotavirus Gastroenteritis, Hemophilus Influenzae type b, Poliomyelitis, Pneumococcal Pneumonia, Measles & Rubella, Cancer of the cervix, Yellow fever, Tuberculosis, Diphtheria, Pertussis (whooping cough), Tetanus and Hepatitis B. Malaria, the fourteenth, is printed as slide text beside the graphic.

'Current Immunization schedule': a grid with one row per vaccine and one column per age (Birth, 6 wks, 10 wks, 14 wks, 5 mo, 6 mo, 7 mo, 8 mo, 9 mo, 12 mo, 15 mo, 18 mo, 22 mo, 24 mo, 10 Yrs, 15-49 Yrs). Dose numbers by row: BCG 1 at birth; Hep B birth dose 1 at birth; Oral polio 0 at birth, 1 at 6 wks, 2 at 10 wks, 3 at 14 wks; DTP-HepB-Hib (penta) 1, 2, 3 at 6, 10, 14 wks; PCV 1, 2, 3 at 6, 10, 14 wks; Rotavirus 1, 2, 3 at 6, 10, 14 wks; Inactivated Polio 1 at 6 wks and 2 at 14 wks; Measles-Rubella 1 at 9 mo and 2 at 18 mo; Yellow Fever 1 at 9 mo; Malaria (row label in red) 1, 2, 3 at 6, 7, 8 mo and 4 at 18 mo; Vitamin A 1 at 6 mo, 2 at 12 mo, 3 at 18 mo, 4 at 24 mo; Deworming 1 at 12 mo; HPV 1 at 10 Yrs; Tetanus Diphtheria (TD) '1,2,3,4 &5' at 15-49 Yrs. The 5 mo, 15 mo and 22 mo columns are empty. Cell shading follows the slide's legend (slide text): dark grey 'previous on schedule'; light blue 'Newly introduced' (Hep B birth dose, IPV 1, Rotavirus 3, Measles-Rubella 2, Yellow Fever); orange 'Yet to be introduced' (Malaria 1 to 4, HPV).

blocks.title: Current Immunization schedule
blocks.content:
Newly introduced
 
Yet to be introduced
 
previous on 
schedule

'Catch up schedule', headed "It is better to vaccinate late than never!". Rows by age: BIRTH (Hep B BD, BCG, OPV0), 6 WEEKS (OPV1, PCV1, DTP1, RV1, IPV1), 10 WEEKS (OPV2, PCV2, DTP2, RV2), 14 WEEKS (OPV3, PCV3, DTP3, RV3, a bar labelled IPV1), 9 MONTHS (MR1, YF), 18 MONTHS (MR2), 2 YEARS. Each vaccine's bar runs down the chart; stop-hand marks end Hep B BD at birth and rotavirus at 2 years. 'When to give': Hep B BD: As soon as possible after birth, ideally within 24 hours and up to 7 days; BCG: As soon as possible after birth; At 6 weeks (or as soon as possible thereafter); At 10 weeks (or as soon as possible thereafter), and at least 4 weeks after dose 1; At 14 weeks (or as soon as possible thereafter), and at least 4 weeks after dose 2; At 9 months (or as soon as possible thereafter); At 18 months (or as soon as possible there after), and at least 4 weeks since the previous dose. 'When not to give': Hep B BD: Not after 7 days; RV1: Not after 2 years of age; Not before 4 weeks has passed since the previous dose, RV2: Not after 2 years of age; Not before 4 weeks has passed since the previous dose, RV3: Not after 2 years of age; Not before 9 months of age (except where indicated)*; MR2: Not before 4 weeks has passed since MR1. Footnote: Even if a long time has passed between doses, there is no need to restart the series from the beginning. There is no upper age limit for most vaccines (except rotavirus < 2years and Hepatitis B BD <7 days).

'Sites of child vaccines': a photograph of a seated baby with labelled arrows. Polio, Vitamin A, Rota (Oral) to the mouth; BCG (Intradermal) and Yellow Fever (Subcutaneous) to the baby's right upper arm; Measles-Rubella (Subcutaneous) to the baby's left upper arm; IPV (2cm apart) (Intramuscular) and PCV (2cm apart) (Intramuscular) to the baby's right thigh; Hep B Birth dose (Intramuscular) and DPT-HepB-Hib (Intramuscular) to the baby's left thigh. Sides are read from the arrows: the baby faces the viewer.

'Life course Immunization performance analysis': a rising staircase of photographs labelled with the share of the population each age group is: At Birth 4.85%, Surviving 4.3%, 9 mths 4.3%, 18 mths 4.3%, 10 year 1.54%, Women 15-49 yrs 23%. Beside the image, as slide text: 'Service Points: 1. Static (At Health Facility) 2. Outreach (Community) 3. School' and 'Immunity Gap approaches: 1. Campaign 2. Routine 3. Outbreak (Covid)'.

'Client Flow at immunization sites': a drawing of a round thatched shelter. Clients come in at 'Entrance', go to 'Waiting, Growth monitoring, screening, Registration in CR, and Health Education', then to 'Vaccintion [sic] Tallying, next appointment Health advice', then leave by 'Check point, health advice, reminder and exit'.

Proposed EIR architecture: 'Existing Birth Registration system (by NIRA)' feeds, through a data-entry step, an 'Electronic Immunization Registry (EIR)' with: Child Identification (Via NIRA/VRS integration); Vaccine Record Module; Scheduling and Reminders; Data Analytics and Reporting. The EIR serves a 'User Interface' for: Healthcare providers; Patients (via app/portal); District/MoH.
